page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. Hardware compute resources consist of an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 256 GB, resulting in an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU density. The instance has no integrated local storage and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, utilizing external storage solutions and network attachments across a 10 Gbps baseline network link. Accelerator hardware such as dedicated GPUs is absent.

The underlying AMD x86_64 architecture incorporates instruction extensions including AVX-512F, AVX-512_VNNI, and AVX-512_BF16, along with cryptographic primitives like VAES and SHA_NI. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong single-core CPU throughput under stress-ng with a score of 3072.68, positioning the instance in the top quartile. Multi-core performance under stress-ng registers at 49143.43, placing it within the median bracket. Memory subsystem testing shows large-block uncached read speeds of 75.61 GB/s and write speeds of 56.11 GB/s, while cached small-block reads achieve 2430.97 GB/s. Data processing metrics include single-threaded gzip compression at 29.13 GB/s and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 174.65 GB/s.

This hardware configuration provides high memory density relative to core count, delivering cost efficiency for processes constrained by memory footprints rather than raw compute cycles. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O must route across remote block storage interfaces. Consequently, the instance is targeted at in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-heavy enterprise database engines, and in-memory analytics workflows.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores paired with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, it features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero integrated local storage, and no GPU hardware. CPU architecture includes AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI and BF16 alongside VAES cryptography. In benchmark evaluations, stress-ng single-core compute performance ranks in the top 25%, while multi-core processing and uncached memory bandwidth (75.61 GB/s read, 56.11 GB/s write) align with mid-range baselines. Without onboard disks, persistence is handled entirely via network storage. The instance matches the requirements of memory-intensive applications, including in-memory caching systems, Redis or Memcached clusters, relational database engines, and analytical data transformation pipelines.
